texts: good. "a second cold snap" is ranked with an ordinal atom and the compound is unpacked into its genus and its "cold" modifier, and the arrival is a plain past event. Same unavoidable caveat as any dated entry here: "day 131 of Year 1" has no day-of-year calendar term, so it lands as a bare (Day 131) beside (Year 1) - a translator-side gap no rewrite fixes.

good. the sharpness state is reified so the time can anchor on it, the flat copular atom is kept beside it, "unusually" becomes its own degree atom rather than being dropped, and "that night" correctly copies day 131 / Year 1 forward from sentence 1.

good. the three lanterns are one counted group sitting on the Cliff Path, the going-out is recorded both as a group event and as a fireable per-lantern rule, and "before dawn" becomes a proper upper time bound. Note only that the per-lantern rule does not carry that dawn bound, so the time limit is queryable off the group event alone.

good. the holding is recorded both as a group event and as a per-lantern rule. Because "their mire-essence" is one per lantern, the "in ..." phrase lives only inside the per-lantern rule - correctly, since a single group-level location would posit one shared mire-essence that is not what you wrote - so a question put to the group event alone will not find where the salt-bloom sat.

mixed: the concessive link is recorded and does point at the right pair of events, but "despite + a noun phrase" is not a shape the instruction set covers - the connective machinery expects two clauses, so the translator has to guess which earlier event the bare noun stands in for. Spell the second clause out and the guess disappears: "The three lanterns went out even though they held salt-bloom."

bad: "recorded the night as an extreme cold event" has no licensed carrier for the "as NP" classification, so the parse improvises in three ways - it treats the night as something the recording changed, it asserts the classification as a plain fact of the night, and it adds a result link saying the recording MADE the night an extreme cold event. Put the classification in a finite that-clause so it is filed as the Council's record rather than as fact: "The Council recorded that the night was an extreme cold event." Separately, "the night" mints a fresh entity with no link back to the "that night" of sentence 2 - only the day-131 dating connects them.

mixed: the report seal, the holder and the addressee are all right, but "four weeks of supply" is a measure-of phrase with no licensed encoding, so the four weeks lands on a dimension no word in the clause supplies - and the same phrase in your other passages lands on a different dimension, so the records will not match each other at query time. Rewrite as "Tessa Brae reported to the Council that the supply in the feather store would last four weeks."

good. "half of the autumn feather store" takes the mass-partitive shape - a portion of the store, with the proportion recorded and the using pointed at that portion - and the store is correctly identified with the feather store of sentence 7. One thing the parse does not carry: the "had used" anteriority, because the sentence names no other event for the using to precede, so nothing orders it against Tessa Brae's report.
good. the past copular wraps the property and attaches it to the same store witness sentence 7 introduced, so the size claim joins the rest of the feather-store record.
